title: Vendor advisory chain: diff the affected/fixed build pair to prove unlisted sibling models still ship the pre-fix code
index_line: T-0014 · MEM_WRITE · advisory affected+fixed build pair → normalized-disassembly diff → patch-absence in unlisted models · corroborated
invariant_violated: A vendor publishes a patch and an affected-model table, and the table is treated as complete: every model shipping the vulnerable binary is assumed listed and fixed. The invariant that actually holds is that models are fixed only when someone ports the patch to their build.

mechanism.does: parse the advisory: the CVE family, the affected product table, and the fixed build identifiers
download the listed model's last-affected and first-fixed builds (the pair the vendor itself published)
unwrap/extract both images (vendor container + filesystem), no execution
disassemble the named daemon in both builds and normalize operands so inserted code does not shift the token stream
sequence-diff the normalized streams -> fixed-only blocks (the patch) and vuln-only blocks (the code the patch removed)
token-match the vuln-only blocks against every unlisted model's daemon, and match the fixed-only blocks too (a real check must not be confused with generic frame arithmetic)
verdict: vuln-only present AND no substantive fixed-only block => unlisted model is unpatched; negative control = the fixed build must clear the vuln-only set

source.protocol.value: the binary that parses attacker packets (the daemon named by the advisory)

sink.memory.copy.value: the size-unchecked copy/copy-family the vendor patch surrounds

guard.signature.value: vendor image wrapper + advisory affected-model table — the scope assumption being tested

size.length.value: packet length / field-length / field-offset checks the patch adds

preconditions.expr: advisory names a CVE family plus affected and fixed builds
the named daemon exists in the target's extracted rootfs and is auto-started
the unlisted model's build date postdates the vendor fix, so absence is not just an older release (grep the image-header version string in the extracted image)
same daemon source generation across builds (compiler signature / source line markers)

spec.method: scan .rodata of both builds for 'GCC: (OpenWrt GCC <ver> <hash>+r#####)' and shared source markers; require the same compiler+r-number family

success: vuln-only blocks from the advisory's affected build present in the unlisted model
fixed-only matches are only generic frame/call setup, no length or offset validation
same compiler signature and source-file markers across builds (same source generation)
failure_like: vuln-only blocks absent => model is not affected or the daemon differs
a substantive fixed-only validation block present => patch was ported, advisory table is fine
false_positive: counting fixed-only matches without reading them (frame-pointer arithmetic matches trivially in every build)
concluding from size or hash differences alone; build hashes always differ
treating a static diff as proof of runtime reachability — it is a patch-absence oracle only

hazards: vendor images are often encrypted: recover the container key with public-key operations only and never claim the vendor's private key was used
the fix may be split across daemons (the advisory's second binary) — check both
an unlisted model may be absent from the table simply because it does not ship the daemon
non_transfers: closed builds where no fixed pair was ever published
daemons rebuilt with different compilers/optimization, where normalization cannot align the streams

evidence.target: public vendor advisory affected/fixed firmware pair (CVE-2025-58455 / CVE-2025-58077)
